message.content:
The value of a U.S. dollar against the British pound fluctuates constantly, so the exact amount can vary from day to day and even minute to minute. As of the most recent market data (mid‑2026), the exchange rate is roughly:

| Currency | Approximate Rate |
|----------|------------------|
| 1 USD →  | 0.77 GBP (≈ £0.77) |

Using that rate:

```
$20 × 0.77 GBP/USD ≈ £15.40
```

So, **$20 is roughly equivalent to £15.4**.  

If you need a precise figure for a specific transaction, it’s best to check a reliable financial news source, a bank’s foreign‑exchange page, or a currency‑conversion tool (e.g., XE.com, OANDA, or your bank’s online portal) at the time of the transaction. These sources will give you the current spot rate and any applicable fees or spreads.
